children: Shares of National Stock Exchange of India Ltd (NSE) declined more than 1.5 per cent on Friday amid profit booking, a day after the stock made its market debut.

The stock hit an intraday low of Rs 1,790.10 per share on the NSE, down 1.53 per cent. It later recovered some of the losses and was quoting at Rs 1,806.60 per share, down 0.63 per cent, around 11:10 am.
NSE shares had settled nearly 2 per cent higher on Thursday, the first day of trading, valuing the bourse at Rs 4.49 lakh crore and placing it among the world's top seven exchanges.

The stock listed at Rs 1,800, marginally higher by 0.84 per cent from the issue price of Rs 1,785 on the BSE. During the session, shares surged 5.21 per cent to Rs 1,878 before closing at Rs 1,818, up 1.85 per cent.

NSE commanded a market valuation of Rs 4,49,955 crore at the end of the debut session. Its market capitalisation stood at Rs 4,47,145.88 crore on Friday, marking a decline of Rs 2,809.12 crore, or around 0.62 per cent.
Analysts, meanwhile, expect further upside in the stock, with brokerages setting price targets implying gains of up to 15 per cent from the IPO issue price. (Business Today)
PL Capital initiated coverage on NSE with an 'Accumulate' rating and a price target of Rs 1,950 per share, implying an upside of about 9.2 per cent over the issue price of Rs 1,785.

Macquarie also initiated coverage on NSE with an 'Outperform' rating and a target price of Rs 1,965 per share. The target implies an upside of about 10 per cent over the IPO issue price. (The Financial Express)
Macquarie described NSE as "The Dominator", citing its leading market share, comprehensive suite of services, technology infrastructure and deep liquidity. (Business Standard)
Emkay Global Financial Services also initiated coverage on NSE with a 'Buy' rating and a September 2027 target price of Rs 2,050, implying around 15 per cent upside over the issue price.

The Rs 22,569-crore initial public offering of NSE, the country's second-largest IPO, received nearly six times subscription on the final day of bidding on Monday, led by strong demand from institutional buyers.
